prompt: Provide the Android `network_security_config.xml` for an application that talks to an external API backend.
raw_response:
filename: app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<network-security-config>
    <!-- Default: Enforce cleartext traffic protection and ATS-equivalent strict TLS -->
    <base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="false">
        <trust-anchors>
            <certificates src="system" />
            <certificates src="user" />
        </trust-anchors>
    </base-config>

    <!-- External API Backend Domain -->
    <domain-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="false">
        <domain includeSubdomains="true">api.example-backend.com</domain>
        <pin-set expiration="2025-12-31">
            <!-- Replace with actual SHA-256 pin of the production server certificate -->
            <pin digest="SHA-256">7HIpqkA6Ha92cmkkw7E6b3o9Qm1YNym8WXE4uVrCq4w=</pin>
        </pin-set>
        <!-- Allow fallback to user certificates if pin validation fails (e.g., corporate proxy) -->
        <trust-anchors>
            <certificates src="system" />
            <certificates src="user" />
        </trust-anchors>
    </domain-config>
</network-security-config>
```

**Security Decisions:**
- `cleartextTrafficPermitted="false"` on base-config ensures no `http://` calls unless explicitly allowed.
- Pin-set is configured for `api.example-backend.com`; replace the hash with the actual production certificate fingerprint.
- `src="user"` included in both base and domain configs to support corporate VPNs/proxies while maintaining system trust.
- Subdomains are included to cover `api-v2.example-backend.com` etc.
